EXTRA CLASS · DINOSAURS · 33 CARDS · AGES 3–5

The Dinosaurs class — every card carries its own move.

Thirty-three dinosaurs, thirty-three ways to move: stomp like a T. rex, make three pretend horns, stretch your neck up high, flap and glide. Every card prints one activity under its name, every dinosaur has its lesson and printable twin right here — and the deck opens with the six dinosaurs everybody asks for first.

Meet the dinosaurs ↓The printable set ↗
HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

Read the card. Do the move. Then go deeper.

Every card in this deck does two jobs: it names one dinosaur and it prints one activity — an “Activity:” line the card means literally. The short pages on this shelf show each card, quote its action word for word, and add one way to make the move into tonight’s game. When one dinosaur becomes a favorite, its lesson page carries the full teaching — what the name means, the facts a grown-up tells, the parent script, the questions to ask — and the library page holds the printable twin with a download button.

The deck opens with the six every child asks for first — the famous red hunter, the three-horned one, the plated one, the tall one, the flyer and the quick one — and then walks the rest of the prehistoric world in file order: armored tanks, trumpet-heads, sail-backs, four-winged gliders and the sea king. For the wild side beyond the Cretaceous, the Animals & Their Habitats class and the Animal Categories class sort today’s animals the same way this deck sorts the ancient ones.

ALL THIRTY-THREE DINOSAURS

Meet the deck — six favorites first.

Every card in the owner’s order: Tyrannosaurus Rex, Triceratops, Stegosaurus, Brachiosaurus, Pterodactyl and Velociraptor lead the way, then the rest of the prehistoric world. Read every card right here on this page.

WHERE THIS CLASS FITS

Beside the habitat class and the animal families.

Dinosaurs sit at one end of the animal story. The Animals & Their Habitats class walks where animals live today — meadow to ocean to ice — and the Animal Categories class sorts every animal family from pets to primates. This deck adds the ancient cast: who the hunters and plant eaters were, and how a body built for one job can become tonight’s game. For more move-like-an-animal play after the deck is done, the Animal Walks rules page on the school’s games shelf turns the same idea into a party game.

Dino moves are real learning. Every stomp, swish and glide on these cards is a body skill in disguise — do the move first, name the facts second, and let the favorite dinosaur pick the order.

TEACHER’S LESSON

How this class is taught.

By the end of this class: your child has met all 33 cards in Dinosaurs, said each word with you and tried one small activity from the lesson.

  1. 01
    Welcome

    “Hello! Today we are learning about Dinosaurs. We have 33 cards, and we will look at them one at a time.”

    How: Sit side by side with the cards in front of you. Keep your voice warm and unhurried, and let your child touch the cards.

  2. Cards 1–10
  3. 02
    Card 1 · Tyrannosaurus Rex

    “Tyrannosaurus Rex! The king of the dinosaurs — roar big, lift your giant foot, and STOMP. One stomp, two stomps — the whole floor shakes!”

    How: Stomp around the room like the biggest dinosaur ever, then shrink: tiptoe like a baby T. rex sneaking up on its dinner. Big feet, little feet, big roar, tiny squeak — the switch is the game.

  4. 03
    Card 2 · Triceratops

    “Triceratops! Three horns — one, two, three! Put your horns on, swing your head gently, and munch, munch, munch the tall grass.”

    How: Point two finger-horns from your forehead and one from your nose, then walk in a slow circle showing them to the whole family. Swap: who can make the proudest triceratops frill with their arms?

  5. 04
    Card 3 · Stegosaurus

    “Stegosaurus! Plates up on your back, spikes ready on your tail — swish, swish, SWISH the tail and keep the bossy dinosaurs away!”

    How: Tuck a scarf or a sock in your waistband as a tail and swish it in big slow arcs. Then freeze like a statue with plates standing tall — can anyone guess which dinosaur you are?

  6. 05
    Card 4 · Brachiosaurus

    “Brachiosaurus! The tall one — stretch your neck up, up, UP to the very tallest leaves. Munch, munch — yummy treetop salad!”

    How: Stretch arms straight up and walk slowly on tiptoe, picking pretend leaves from door frames and lampshades. Then crouch low and pick grass like a little dinosaur — tall stretch, small nibble, tall stretch again.

  7. 06
    Card 5 · Pterodactyl

    “Pterodactyl! Wings out, flap, flap, flap — and GLIDE! Soar over the mountains, dip down low, and scoop a fish right out of the water!”

    How: Flap five times, then hold still and glide across the rug. Land on a "cliff" (the couch arm), then take off again. Score one point per glide that ends softly.

  8. 07
    Card 6 · Velociraptor

    “Velociraptor! Quick, quick, quick — three fast dino steps, then FREEZE. Where did everybody go? A raptor has fast feet and fast eyes!”

    How: Run three quick steps, freeze, look left and right, then three more. Play it as a race across the room — first one to the far wall with three freezes on the way is the champion raptor.

  9. 08
    Card 7 · Allosaurus

    “Allosaurus! A big hunter with a bigger mouth — take a deep breath and ROAR one giant roar... and now the biggest roar of all. ROOOAR!”

    How: Roar once facing the window, once facing the door. Then whisper both roars — baby allosaurus size. Loud, louder, tiny: the volume switch is what makes roaring a real game.

  10. 09
    Card 8 · Ankylosaurus

    “Ankylosaurus! Armor on your back, club on your tail — swing it sloooowly around... thud! Nobody bothers an ankylosaurus twice!”

    How: Hold a soft cushion as your club and swing it in a slow semicircle around your feet. Then sit down, tuck in like the armored ball the card shows, and see who can guess what you are.

  11. 10
    Card 9 · Archaeopteryx

    “Archaeopteryx! Half dinosaur, half bird — stretch your feathered wings out wiiide... flap a little... glide a little. The very first flying cousin!”

    How: Stretch both arms out like wings, then bow one wing at a time to each side. Flap three small flutters, then glide to a perch. Feathers on your head add instant archaeopteryx power.

  12. 11
    Card 10 · Baryonyx

    “Baryonyx! The fish catcher — dip your claw in the river, wait... wait... SWOOSH! A fish for lunch! Snap, munch, yummy!”

    How: Stand on one leg as the riverbank, dip one hand low, hold perfectly still for three seconds, then scoop the fish up and gobble it. Alternating hands keeps the fishing trip going all afternoon.

  13. Cards 11–20
  14. 12
    Card 11 · Carnotaurus

    “Carnotaurus! The bull-headed hunter — put your two horns on, lower your head, and POSE. Fierce face... prouder face... the fiercest face of all!”

    How: Point two fingers above your eyebrows, lower your head and strike three poses: fierce, proud, silly. Everyone else copies the pose — the silliest pose gets the biggest roar.

  15. 13
    Card 12 · Centrosaurus

    “Centrosaurus! One strong horn on your nose, a big frill behind your head — make a gentle horn pose and nod hello to the whole herd.”

    How: Touch your nose-horn forward, hold your arm-frill up and walk a slow herd circle with everyone else posing too. Gentle is the rule: the pose is for saying hello, not for bumping.

  16. 14
    Card 13 · Ceratosaurus

    “Ceratosaurus! A hunter with a tiny horn on its nose — tap your nose, make your horn, and pose with your proudest hunter face.”

    How: Tap the tip of your nose for the horn, strike a pose, then stomp three steps and pose again. The game is posing in new places: doorway pose, couch pose, window pose.

  17. 15
    Card 14 · Compsognathus

    “Compsognathus! The littlest hunter — tiny steps now: one, two, three, four, five! Small feet, quick eyes, and off you scoot!”

    How: Take five tiptoe steps, freeze, then five more. Try five tiny steps backward, five sideways, five in a circle. Little dinosaurs can go anywhere — quietly.

  18. 16
    Card 15 · Corythosaurus

    “Corythosaurus! A trumpet on its head — take a deep breath and call the herd: TOOOTO! Long and low, loud and proud!”

    How: Hands cupped around your mouth as the crest, make one long trumpet note, then three short ones. The herd answers: everyone else echoes the call back — long, short, short.

  19. 17
    Card 16 · Deinonychus

    “Deinonychus! Quick feet, big claw — run-run-run, JUMP, and freeze with your claws up! The fastest hunter in the forest is you!”

    How: Take six quick steps, jump high with both claw-hands up, and freeze like a statue. Do it across the whole room — the jump-freeze at the end is the part everyone repeats.

  20. 18
    Card 17 · Diplodocus

    “Diplodocus! Long neck one way, long tail the other — stretch up high and munch the leaves... now swish that long tail behind you!”

    How: Stand tall, reach one arm up as the neck and let the other arm trail as the tail, then walk a slow loop around the room. Swap ends: now the tail arm leads and the neck arm follows.

  21. 19
    Card 18 · Euoplocephalus

    “Euoplocephalus! Armor all over — curl in small, tuck your head, hide under your shields. Nobody can find you now!”

    How: Curl up small on the floor with your arms tucked in — count to five all tucked — then unfold into a giant armored dinosaur and stomp twice. Curl, count, unfold: the safest game in the deck.

  22. 20
    Card 19 · Giganotosaurus

    “Giganotosaurus! Even bigger than a T. rex — three GIANT steps: one... two... three! Can your giant steps cross the whole room?”

    How: Take three giant steps from one wall and see where you land, then three more. Measure: how many giant steps does the hallway take? A baby giga takes baby steps — tiny ones still count.

  23. 21
    Card 20 · Hadrosaurus

    “Hadrosaurus! A duck bill for a mouth — nibble, nibble, nibble the leaves. Small bites, chomp chomp — a plant eater is always polite at lunch!”

    How: Pick pretend leaves at three heights — low grass, bush height, up on tiptoe — and nibble each one with different sounds. Finish with one big happy chomp and a satisfied dinosaur sigh.

  24. Cards 21–30
  25. 22
    Card 21 · Iguanodon

    “Iguanodon! Reach out with your hand, grab the branch, and MUNCH munch munch. Thumbs up, spike ready — nobody pushes an iguanodon around!”

    How: Reach one arm out, strip pretend leaves off with your other hand, and munch with big exaggerated chews. Give a thumbs-up spike at the end — the iguanodon signature.

  26. 23
    Card 22 · Maiasaura

    “Maiasaura! The mummy dinosaur — cuddle your baby dino, feed it leaves, and pat, pat, pat it to sleep. A good mother makes a warm nest!”

    How: Cuddle a stuffed animal as the baby, pretend-feed it leaves, tuck it into a cushion nest and pat its head five times. Then swap: your child is the baby being cared for — giggles guaranteed.

  27. 24
    Card 23 · Microraptor

    “Microraptor! Four little wings — flap, flap, flap them fast! Small wings, shiny feathers, and off it glides between the trees!”

    How: Flap hands and feet together for three seconds — four wings working — then hold a glide pose with arms and legs spread. Jump from cushion to cushion as tree to tree.

  28. 25
    Card 24 · Mosasaurus

    “Mosasaurus! The king of the ancient sea — arms out, swim, swim, swim... dive deep, then SNAP those long jaws at a fishy lunch!”

    How: Lie on your tummy and do one big swimming stroke, arms sweeping wide, then pop up for a jaw-snap. Glide around the room like the sea is everywhere — the floor counts as ocean.

  29. 26
    Card 25 · Ouranosaurus

    “Ouranosaurus! A sail on its back — arch up tall and make your sail BIGGER... and bigger! Look at that sail catching the sunshine!”

    How: Arch your back and stretch your arms behind as the sail, growing taller and taller until the sail is enormous — then flop flat like a tired dinosaur and start again.

  30. 27
    Card 26 · Oviraptor

    “Oviraptor! The nest keeper — curl your arms around your egg and keep it safe. Gentle wings over the egg... shhh, the baby is sleeping!”

    How: Cup your hands as the egg, then wrap both arms around it and stand guard, walking in slow circles around the nest. Someone else tries a gentle "steal" — the guardian shields without letting go.

  31. 28
    Card 27 · Pachycephalosaurus

    “Pachycephalosaurus! A helmet made of bone — pat your round head, stand tall, and bump very gently: boop! Gentle bumps only — we are friendly dinosaurs!”

    How: Stand on one leg, pat your dome head twice, then lean in for a gentle shoulder bump with a partner — boop! The softest bump wins the boss crown.

  32. 29
    Card 28 · Parasaurolophus

    “Parasaurolophus! A horn growing from its head — breathe in deep and call: HOOOOONK! Can the herd hear you from far, far away?”

    How: Rest one forearm along the back of your head as the crest, breathe in and make one long deep honk. The herd answers with its own honks — first loud, then whisper-honks for the evening.

  33. 30
    Card 29 · Plateosaurus

    “Plateosaurus! One of the very first long necks — stand up tall, reach out your arm, and pick the very tallest leaves. Higher... higher... you got one!”

    How: Pick three pretend leaves at three heights: knee, shoulder and tiptoe-reach. Munch each one twice, then bend down and graze like a four-legged dinosaur — the same animal, two feeding styles.

  34. 31
    Card 30 · Quetzalcoatlus

    “Quetzalcoatlus! The giant of the sky — big slow flaps, then a loooong glide. Such a big flyer does not need to hurry!”

    How: Take three enormous slow flaps, then glide with arms spread for five whole seconds. Land tall on straight legs — a giant pterosaur walks proudly, then takes off again.

  35. Cards 31–33
  36. 32
    Card 31 · Spinosaurus

    “Spinosaurus! A sail as big as a door on its back — lift your arms up high and make YOUR big sail. Now snap that long snout at a fish!”

    How: Sweep both arms up behind your head into one big sail shape, hold it tall, then flop into a swim and snap your snout hands three times. Sail, swim, snap — the spinosaurus routine.

  37. 33
    Card 32 · Styracosaurus

    “Styracosaurus! A crown of spikes around your frill — spread your spike-arms, lift your head, and make the bravest horn pose of all!”

    How: Fan your fingers out around your head as the spikes, take one big brave step forward and hold the pose for three seconds. Then shuffle sideways in a herd line, poses up, no bumping.

  38. 34
    Card 33 · Therizinosaurus

    “Therizinosaurus! The longest claws in the world — stretch your arms out and show those giant claws... so long! So wavy! And still a gentle leaf eater!”

    How: Extend both arms wide, curl your fingers into long pretend claws and wave them slowly like feather dusters. Then hook an invisible high branch and pull down a leafy breakfast.

  39. 35
    Practice

    “Now you are the teacher! Pick any card and tell me what it is.”

    How: Let your child choose the card and say the word in their own way. Teaching someone else is the strongest way to remember.

  40. 36
    Check

    “Can you find Tyrannosaurus Rex? Now show me Diplodocus.”

    How: A point, a fetch or the word all count as a pass. If they are unsure, name it for them and try again another day — there are no scores and no pressure.

  41. 37
    Well done

    “Well done! Today we met 33 cards. Let us look for one of them at home.”

    How: End on a win, then spot one of the words in real life today. Meeting it again in the real world is what makes it stay.

Read the script while you show the cards — the say-lines are yours to say out loud and the how-lines are the activity behind each step. Skip, shorten or repeat anything: the class bends to your child, never the other way round.
